ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a black dot representing a horizontal frictionless axle/rotating shaft, and the outer ring is a thin black circular rim; three orange uniform spokes extend from the rotating shaft, separated from one another by 120°. One of the spokes points horizontally to the left, and the other two are symmetrically inclined up and down on the right side, one toward the upper right and one toward the lower right. Each spoke is labeled with mass M and length R, and the rim mass is negligible. Reasoning: The weight Mg of each uniform spoke acts at its midpoint, at a distance R/2 from the rotating shaft. Taking counterclockwise as positive, gravity is vertically downward, so the torque about the rotating shaft is τ_z = x F_y = x(-Mg) = -Mg x_cm. The horizontal spoke on the left has center-of-mass x-coordinate x_cm = -R/2, so the torque is +MgR/2. The upper-right and lower-right spokes are respectively +60° and -60° relative to the positive x direction, and their center-of-mass x-coordinates are both x_cm = (R/2)cos60° = R/4, so each produces torque -MgR/4. The total torque is +MgR/2 - MgR/4 - MgR/4 = 0.

raw_record.question_text: A wheel consists of three uniform spokes, with length \( R \) and mass \( M \), mounted 120 degrees apart on a horizontal frictionless axle and connected by a rim of negligible mass. Consider the counterclockwise direction to be positive. When the spokes are oriented as shown in the diagram, what is the net torque on the wheel due to the weight of the spokes?

method.method_draft: Direct signed-torque summation. First read the diagram: the black dot is the axle, with three orange uniform spokes; one spoke is horizontal to the left, and the other two are symmetric on the right, one slanting upward and one downward, 120° apart. From the text, each spoke has mass M and length R, the rim is negligible, and counterclockwise torque is positive. Treat each uniform spoke’s weight Mg as acting at its midpoint, R/2 from the axle. Use τ_z = xF_y since gravity is vertical downward, so τ = -Mg x_cm. The left horizontal spoke has x_cm = -R/2, giving +MgR/2. Each right slanted spoke has x_cm = (R/2)cos60° = R/4, giving -MgR/4 each. Add the three torques: +MgR/2 - MgR/4 - MgR/4 = 0.
method.CoT_raw:

推理：每根均匀辐条的重力 Mg 作用在其中点，距离转轴 R/2。取逆时针为正，重力竖直向下，所以关于转轴的力矩为 τ_z = x F_y = x(-Mg) = -Mg x_cm。左侧水平辐条的质心横坐标 x_cm = -R/2，因此力矩为 +MgR/2。右上和右下两根辐条相对正 x 方向分别为 +60° 和 -60°，它们的质心横坐标均为 x_cm = (R/2)cos60° = R/4，因此每根产生力矩 -MgR/4。总力矩为 +MgR/2 - MgR/4 - MgR/4 = 0。

method.method_draft: Equivalent center-of-mass method. First read the diagram: the three orange spokes radiate from the central black axle at equal 120° angular spacing, with the left spoke balanced by two symmetric right-side spokes. From the text, the three spokes are identical uniform rods and the rim has negligible mass. For each spoke, its own center of mass lies halfway along the spoke, so the three spoke-center vectors have equal magnitudes R/2 and directions 120° apart. The vector sum of three equal vectors 120° apart is zero, so the combined center of mass of the three spokes is exactly at the axle. In a uniform gravitational field, the net gravitational torque about the axle equals the torque of the total weight acting at the combined center of mass. Since that point is at the axle, the lever arm is zero, so the net torque is 0.

claims.claim: In this problem, when gravity has only a vertical component, the torque about the rotation axis can be written as τ_z = x F_y.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Gravity is vertically downward, so the torque about the rotation axis is τ_z = x F_y

claims.claim: The vertical component of gravity is F_y = -Mg.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: x(-Mg)

claims.claim: The gravitational torque about the rotation axis can be written as τ_z = -Mg x_cm.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: τ_z = x F_y = x(-Mg) = -Mg x_cm

claims.claim: The x-coordinate of the center of mass of the left horizontal spoke is x_cm = -R/2.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The x-coordinate of the center of mass of the left horizontal spoke is x_cm = -R/2

claims.claim: The torque of the left horizontal spoke is +MgR/2.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore the torque is +MgR/2

claims.claim: The upper-right spoke is at +60° relative to the positive x direction.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The upper-right and lower-right two spokes are respectively at +60° and -60° relative to the positive x direction

claims.claim: The lower-right spoke is at -60° relative to the positive x direction.

claims.source: The upper-right and lower-right two spokes are respectively at +60° and -60° relative to the positive x direction

claims.claim: The x-coordinate of the center of mass of the upper-right spoke is x_cm = (R/2)cos60° = R/4.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Their x-coordinates of the centers of mass are both x_cm = (R/2)cos60° = R/4

claims.claim: The x-coordinate of the center of mass of the lower-right spoke is x_cm = (R/2)cos60° = R/4.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Their x-coordinates of the centers of mass are both x_cm = (R/2)cos60° = R/4

claims.claim: The upper-right spoke produces a torque of -MgR/4.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore each one produces a torque of -MgR/4.

claims.claim: The lower-right spoke produces a torque of -MgR/4.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore each one produces a torque of -MgR/4.

claims.claim: The total torque is +MgR/2 - MgR/4 - MgR/4 = 0.
claims.label: reasoning
